units.source_text: 匂亲王打算今天再在这里游玩一天，但京中又派中宫大夫带了许多殿上人来迎接他回宫。

en.t: Prince Niou meant to spend another day here in pleasure, but from the capital the Middle Captain of the Empress's Household was again sent with many courtiers to escort him back to the palace.

units.source_text: 他心慌意乱，懊恨千万，实在不想回京。

en.t: His heart was in turmoil, he was full of bitter regret, and he truly did not want to return to the capital.

units.source_text: 便写一封信给二女公子，信中并无一句言情抒怀的话，只是老老实实、详详细细地叙述感想。

en.t: He therefore wrote a letter to the Second Princess, but in it there was not a single word of love or outpouring of feeling; he only set down his thoughts honestly and in full detail.

units.source_text: 二女公子推想匂皇子左右人目繁多，事端纷忙，故并不作复。

en.t: The Second Princess supposed that Prince Niou was surrounded by too many watchful eyes and too many pressing affairs, and so she sent no reply.

units.source_text: 她只是更加确信：像她这样微不足数的人，高攀尊贵的皇子，毕竟是不相称的。

en.t: She only became more certain that for someone as insignificant as herself to reach up toward so noble a prince was, after all, unsuitable.

units.source_text: 以前远居两地，阔别多时，因而苦思劳盼，原是应有之事；

en.t: Before, when they lived far apart in two places and had long been separated, it was only natural that she should pine for him and wait in longing;

units.source_text: 今见命驾而来，心中正感喜慰，岂知只在附近喧嚣取乐而过门不入。

en.t: now, seeing that he had ordered his carriage and come, her heart was just beginning to feel joy and comfort, but who could have known he would merely make merry nearby and pass her gate without entering.

units.source_text: 这便使得二女公子痛心疾首，方寸恼乱了。

en.t: This left the Second Princess heartsick and deeply distressed, her whole mind thrown into painful confusion.

units.source_text: 匂亲王更是忧愁苦闷，无限伤心。

en.t: Prince Niou, for his part, was even more sorrowful and tormented, with grief beyond measure.

units.source_text: 左右欲请皇子欣赏鱼梁上的冰鱼，取了许多，陈列在色彩或深或浅的红叶上，以供观赏。

en.t: His attendants, wishing the prince to admire the icefish from the fish weir, caught many of them and arranged them on maple leaves of varying deep and pale colors for him to view.

units.source_text: 随从人等都极口称赞。

en.t: All the people in attendance praised the display to the utmost.

units.source_text: 匂亲王也跟着众人漫步闲玩，然而自己心情郁结，愁绪填胸，常常茫然地怅望天空。

en.t: Prince Niou also wandered along with the others in idle amusement, yet his own heart was heavy and filled with sorrow, and he often gazed blankly and wistfully up at the sky.

units.source_text: 遥见八亲王山庄中的树梢，姿态特别优美。

en.t: In the distance he could see the treetops at Prince Hachi's mountain villa, and their forms were especially graceful.

units.source_text: 缠附在常青树上的常春藤的颜色也富有意趣，远看竟有凄凉之感。

en.t: The colors of the ivy twining around the evergreen trees were also full of charm, and from afar they even gave a sense of desolation.

units.source_text: 薰中纳言也很懊丧：预先写信通知她们，反而弄得没趣。

en.t: Kaoru, the Middle Counselor, was also greatly dejected: by writing ahead to notify them, he had instead made the occasion awkward and disappointing.

units.source_text: 去春随匂亲王游宇治的诸公子，想起了八亲王邸内樱花的美色，共话八亲王死后两位女公子的孤寂。

en.t: The young nobles who had accompanied Prince Niou to Uji the previous spring remembered the beauty of the cherry blossoms at Prince Hachi's residence and spoke together of the loneliness of the two princesses after his death.

units.source_text: 其中也有人隐约闻知匂亲王与二女公子私通之事。

en.t: Among them were some who had vaguely heard of the secret affair between Prince Niou and the Second Princess.

units.source_text: 但也有全不知情的人。

en.t: But there were also people who knew nothing of it at all.

units.source_text: 总之，人生之事，无论这般那般，即使发生在这种荒山僻处，也自会传闻于世。

en.t: In short, the affairs of human life, whatever form they take, will naturally become known in the world even when they occur in such a remote mountain place.

units.source_text: 他们众口一词地说：“这两位女公子长得十分美貌，并且是弹筝妙手。

en.t: They all said with one voice, "These two princesses are exceedingly beautiful, and they are also masters at playing the koto.

units.source_text: 因为八亲王在世之时，朝朝夜夜教导她们。”

en.t: That is because Prince Hachi taught them morning and night while he was still alive."

units.source_text: 宰相中将遂赋诗曰：

en.t: The Consultant Captain then composed a poem, saying:
